header.stance: 油價走低帶動實質殖利率下降，美債漲勢擴大

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價續跌，美債漲勢由短端擴及中長天期

荷莫茲海峽油輪通行增加、能源出口逐步恢復，減輕了市場對供給長期受阻的擔憂，週三美債各天期普遍上漲。5年期殖利率下降10個基點至4.17%，表現最佳；10年期下降9個基點至4.41%。即使美國原油庫存大幅減少，油價仍下跌約4%，住宅資料不如預期，也顯示利率敏感產業正在降溫。

與週二由2年期領漲不同，這次實質殖利率也加入跌勢。10年期實質殖利率下降6個基點至2.23%，損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點至2.18%，共同推動名目殖利率走低。2年期僅下降5個基點至4.11%，曲線因而趨平。$700億5年期標售獲得相當程度的投資人承接，沒有打斷漲勢。

公司債供給仍在加速。美國6月投資級發債已達$1,750億，超過6月歷史紀錄及交易商原先估計，還有大型科技融資案正在準備。不過，各發行人的條件差異很大：Hertz尋求以債付息的可轉債融資，Shapoorji Pallonji要求展延，Antolin則讓債權人在延後收款與削減本金之間選擇。美債殖利率下降有利投資級債券報酬，高收益債ETF卻幾乎持平。

## 5年期買盤消化供給，實質殖利率同步下降

5年期美債漲幅超過短端與長債，30年期殖利率下降8個基點至4.86%。2年與10年期利差收窄4個基點至30，2年與30年期收窄3個基點至75，扭轉了週二買盤集中短端時的陡峭化走勢。5及7年期實質殖利率分別下降5與6個基點，至1.98%及2.09%；20與30年期則下降6與5個基點，至2.53%及2.71%。

住宅資料讓債市多了一個油價以外的支撐。5月新屋銷售不理想，建築許可也低於預期。單一產業尚不足以代表全面衰退，但接在前一天企業活動加速、就業轉弱的調查之後，住宅降溫使投資人更願意接受較低的實質殖利率。2年期跌幅較小，仍保留了Fed繼續升息的可能。

$700億5年期公債最高得標殖利率為4.200%，票息4.125%，投標倍數2.35。間接投標人取得$430.28億，直接投標人取得$178.20億，一級交易商承接競爭性得標額中的$90.06億。這筆大額供給有相當程度由投資人吸收。

較短天期的供給同樣找到買盤。$280億浮動利率券續發最高得標折價利差為0.079%，利差0.103%，投標倍數2.99；間接投標人取得$186.50億，交易商$93.31億，直接投標人沒有得標。$690億119天期國庫券最高得標折價利率3.770%，換算投資利率3.871%，投標倍數2.55；間接投標人的$374.14億承接額，高於交易商的$284.95億。

4至13週期國庫券殖利率持平，17週期息票等值殖利率上升2個基點至3.87%，26及52週期則分別下降1與2個基點，至3.94%及3.98%。浮動利率券6月26日交割，119天期國庫券與5年期公債6月30日交割。當天投標順暢，相關資金移轉仍在後面。

Fed一位經濟學家的研究，則呈現美債流動性背後更大的槓桿部位。截至2025年9月，以附買回融資持有現券、搭配期貨的基差交易，估計約$8,300億，占避險基金美債多頭曝險35%。基金美債總曝險在兩年間倍增至$4兆，最大50家控制其中90%。即使平時標售順利，這類規模龐大且集中的部位，仍可能在保證金或波動率突然上升時放大衝擊。

## 投資級發債創紀錄，弱勢借款人的條件更艱難

美國6月投資級發行已達$1,750億，比2025年整個6月多60%，並突破2020年的6月紀錄；輝達與SpaceX各占$250億。交易商原本預估本月約$1,300億，如今總額甚至可能超過$2,000億。年初以來發行達$1.15兆，追平2020年同期速度。信用利差偏窄，抵銷部分較高基準利率的成本；Fed可能升息，也促使企業提早鎖定資金。

後續融資規模依然可觀。NTT正在準備約$100億多幣別債券，字節跳動考慮約$200億境外貸款，同時評估今年最高$700億AI支出。兩案都尚未有最終條件或實際訂單簿。SK海力士則計畫發行韓元45.45兆、約合$294億的Nasdaq存託憑證，預計7月10日開始交易。股權融資可以減少眼前新增負債的需要，整個投資週期的資金規模仍在擴張。

紐約Fed的6月公司債市場壓力指數更新，也顯示整體運作尚稱順暢。全市場指標改善至略高於歷史第20百分位，投資級約在第50百分位，高收益債壓力仍處歷史低檔。指數同時納入初級市場、次級流動性與有無成交債券等資訊，觀察範圍比單日ETF報酬更廣。當天LQD上漲0.46%，HYG與JNK分別小跌0.03%及0.06%。

部分買方也願意用較低流動性換取收益。Clearwater Analytics逾400家企業客戶管理約$1兆資產，企業財務主管持有Rule 144A債券的中位比重，已由數年前接近零升至2%；相較類似公開投資級債券，平均殖利率多約52個基點。連以現金管理為主的投資組合，也逐步增加這類配置。

### 展延與融資結構反映個別壓力

Hertz計畫搭配$3億以債付息的可轉債，以及供可轉債投資人放空的$1億股票。部分循環額度6月到期，以新增債務支付利息有助保留現金。公司警告第2季調整後獲利不會超過$8,000萬後，股價下跌41%。方案提供資金，也帶來潛在股權稀釋與未來債務增加。

Shapoorji Pallonji集團提出30個基點同意費，希望把1,430億盧比零息債從6月30日起至少展延1個月，另要求把Porteast Investment的一項債務條件延至9月。後者另筆$34億貸款的貸款價值比上限，先前已暫時由34%提高至40%。借款以集團持有的18.4% Tata Sons股權擔保，因此抵押品價值直接影響協商空間。

這些融資原本就不便宜。Goswami零息券在2023年發行時殖利率18.75%，當時是印度最大高收益債交易；目前本金降至834.2億盧比，殖利率卻升至21.75%。Porteast的$34億貸款原定價19.75%，債權人包括Ares、Cerberus、Davidson Kempner、Farallon及德意志銀行。多數貸款人支持展延，Ares仍在協商，30個基點費用尚未換得全體同意。

Antolin則針對逾€10億、約合$11億債務提供兩條路。債權人可保留全額本金，改為2035年到期、票息6.97%、期間不攤還；或接受2030年到期及8.28%票息，但只保留現有債券面額的67.5%。希望保全本金的銀行貸款人，還須分攤€2.2億新增營運資金。保全債權意味著等待更久，接受減記則換取較早還款與較高票息。

基礎建設借款人仍能以實體資產取得私募資金。Terawatt安排5年期優先有擔保額度，上限$3億，初始額度$1.5億，另有同額擴充選項，用於充電場站，服務客戶包括Waymo。BloombergNEF估計，全球充電網路至2040年需要逾$6,350億。Stonepeak另發行約$25億私募債，為一座路易斯安那州LNG出口站的建造融資再融資，並已同意買入該站40%權益。兩案雖有具體資產支撐，仍取決於開發、使用率與完工進度。

## 能源壓力減輕，各國央行仍保留升息方向

ECB執委Isabel Schnabel表示，要讓通膨回到2%，可能仍須進一步升息，幅度與時點取決於衝突、成長及物價。她指出，現貨能源仍高於戰前水準，遠期成本也偏高。拉加德認為目前不必更強烈回應，兩者之間仍容得下循序調整，而非加速緊縮。

德國ifo企業景氣指數由85.0小升至85.6。現況改善，預期也不再那麼悲觀，但製造業訂單再次下降，服務、貿易與建築改善程度不一。這份調查減輕了眼前衰退疑慮，仍不足以說明復甦已經強勁。

日本6月會議意見摘要更明確支持繼續正常化。先前以7比1將政策利率升至1%、創1995年以來最高後，委員仍認為金融情勢寬鬆、基礎通膨接近2%。一位委員估計中性利率約2%，位於央行1.1%至2.5%的估計區間內；另一位傾向每隔數月考慮升息。總裁植田和男提醒通膨可能超標，步調須視經濟、物價與金融狀況而定。日圓升息後仍接近多年低點，輸入性通膨與可能干預匯市的風險持續存在。

澳洲央行副總裁Andrew Hauser認為，經濟已來到菲利普斯曲線較陡的部分，較快升息可能以較小的就業代價壓低通膨。RBA在今年前3次會議升息後，暫停於4.35%；其預測仍要到2028年中，通膨才回到2%至3%目標的中點，失業率最高達4.7%，因此仍可能再次升息。

韓國央行則同時關注物價、房市與信用。政策利率自2025年下半年維持2.5%，但隨首爾地區房價、家庭債務及槓桿投資再度累積失衡，央行表示須在適當時機升息。銀行與非銀行機構仍有符合監理要求的資本與流動性緩衝，風險主要在槓桿資產價格反轉時，脆弱借款人與非銀行融資可能承壓，需要搭配審慎監理措施。

新加坡與泰國的眼前壓力較小。新加坡5月核心通膨維持1.4%，低於調查預估的1.6%，支持7月按兵不動；此前4月已緊縮貨幣政策，並把2026年核心通膨預測區間提高至1.5%至2.5%。泰國5月通膨降至2.79%、匯率相對穩定，市場預期維持1天期附買回利率1%。其央行過去也曾先觀察供給因素造成的通膨，再決定升息。

加拿大的討論則在於行動太早或太晚各有風險。第1季實質GDP年化萎縮0.1%，接續第4季下降1%，但過半產業仍成長、消費支出上升，決策者認為疲弱範圍不足以構成衰退。央行維持2.25%，核心指標接近2%，能源傳導有限。若油價已恢復正常才升息，可能過度反應；若價格傳導持續，延後行動又可能增加後續代價。

歐洲政府另獲有限財政彈性，可運用原本為國防設計的豁免條款，進行能源韌性投資，但3%赤字上限及各國支出路徑仍保留。信評分析師認為調整範圍有限，尚不至於明顯損害信用品質。然而，2026年全球主權借款預估達$14.1兆，ECB正在縮減持債，荷蘭退休基金也減少長天期曝險，增加的供給仍須由市場承接。

## 阿根廷累積7月還款資金，墨西哥通膨低於預期

阿根廷財政部已累積約$36億美元存款，可支應7月9日$42億債券款項的約85%。經濟部長Luis Caputo籌得硬通貨的平均成本為6.7%，低於目前直接在國際市場交易約9%的成本，也低於數月前約10%。本地美元債、向央行購匯及多邊機構支持的融資，使政府不必立刻依靠國際發債。

較低成本並未消除後續到期壓力。本地美元債將在2027與2028年到期，披索標售固定利率約20%、實質利率約7%。另有法令授權最高$50億、由世界銀行及美洲開發銀行等機構支持的美元借款，估計成本接近6%，授權與實際收到資金仍有區別。國家風險降至約430個基點，比先前至少低100個基點，讓未來重返市場的成本條件有所改善。

墨西哥6月上半月通膨低於預期。整體物價年增3.55%，調查中位數為3.72%；核心放緩至4.12%，接近預估4.13%。低於預期的部分主要來自核心以外。政策利率6.50%、2026年成長預測由1.6%降至1.1%的背景下，資料讓Banxico較有空間等待，但核心物價仍偏高。

智利在燃料成本大幅增加、通膨超標後，維持利率4.5%。5月物價月增0.2%，只有調查預期的一半，官員仍預估2027年第2季回到3%通膨。印度央行總裁則表示，現在討論升息為時過早，帶動10年期公債殖利率下降5個基點至6.82%。截至6月22日，季風降雨仍比正常少43%，糧食價格風險尚在。

Pimco認為，中國製造業過剩產能可能為新興市場本幣債提供較長期支撐。貿易障礙讓更多中國出口轉向發展中經濟體，較便宜商品有助壓低通膨，增加降息空間。該公司結合較高實質殖利率與穩健政策架構，偏好拉丁美洲，特別是巴西、哥倫比亞與秘魯。不過，進口成本下降也讓本地製造商面臨競爭，美元走強仍可能抵銷利多。週三EMB上漲0.32%，美債殖利率下降的助益超過美元小升的壓力。

## 油輪通行恢復，影響大於美國原油去庫存

WTI下跌3.92%至$70.34，布蘭特下跌4.33%至$73.74，一個月跌幅擴大至27.18%及28.78%。美伊表示談判取得進展，更多油輪穿越荷莫茲海峽；阿聯6月初出口已恢復至戰前近85%，卡達也預期未受損LNG產能在數週內回到正常。談判仍未定案，實際運輸與產能的恢復已讓市場有更多供給改善的依據。

EIA公布商業原油庫存減少610萬桶，降至4.121億桶，比5年同期平均低約7%。成品油卻累庫：汽油增加210萬桶、餾分油增加310萬桶，煉油廠產能利用率達96.1%。4週平均汽油需求比去年同期低3.0%，總成品油供應則增加2.1%。這些細節使原油去庫存所呈現的供給緊張訊號不那麼單純。

週二重挫後，股市當天跌幅溫和。S&P 500下跌0.10%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.43%，半導體股小跌0.18%，VIX下降4.41%至18.63。美債漲勢擴大的同時，股市避險需求反而降低，較符合能源壓力緩解，而非新一波衰退恐慌。

美元指數上升0.20%至101.61，一週上漲1.52%。黃金下跌3.38%至$3,990.30，銅價下跌1.9%至每噸$13,117.50，美元走強與Fed偏鷹預期對金屬不利。美債殖利率下降，並未同時帶來美元轉弱或商品全面反彈。

## 中天期領漲後，接續檢驗PCE與7年期供給

6月25日美東時間8:30，美國將公布5月PCE通膨、個人所得與支出、耐久財訂單、第1季GDP第3次估計及初領失業救濟金。住宅資料轉弱、實質殖利率加入跌勢後，物價與消費資料將顯示，買盤擴及中長天期是否還有油價以外的基本面支撐。若核心價格壓力持續，漲幅最大的中天期將更受檢視。

財政部11:30標售$700億4週期及$750億8週期國庫券，13:00接續標售$440億7年期公債，13:40至14:00買回剩餘天期20至30年的名目附息券。標售券6月30日交割。投標參與與交易商承接比例，將提供與週三5年期結果的下一個比較，實際交割資金流則在稍後。

ECB經濟公報於6月25日中歐夏令時間10:00公布；Banxico在美東15:00宣布決策，目前隔夜利率6.50%。6月26日日本時間8:30，再公布東京6月CPI初值。這些資訊將補充歐洲能源價格傳導、墨西哥如何回應整體通膨放緩，以及日本持續正常化背後的物價情勢。

overall_summary.headline: 油價回落，美債漲勢擴大；6月投資級供給創紀錄
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷莫茲海峽油輪通行與出口恢復，使油價下跌約4%，美債買盤由短端擴大。5年期殖利率下降10個基點至4.17%，10年期下降9個基點至4.41%。與週二不同，實質殖利率也帶來助益：10年期實質殖利率下降6個基點至2.23%，通膨補償下降3個基點至2.18%。住宅資料疲弱，另提供美國內需降溫的訊號。

$700億5年期標售在4.200%取得相當程度的直接及間接投標人承接。美國6月投資級發債達$1,750億，超過交易商預期，NTT與字節跳動還在準備或考慮更多融資。弱勢企業條件較艱難：Hertz尋求以債付息的可轉債，Shapoorji Pallonji要求展延，Antolin則提供不同天期、票息與本金回收組合。

能源走低尚未消除海外政策分歧。ECB與日本央行仍保留升息方向，加拿大成長與新加坡通膨則容許較多等待。阿根廷存款已可支應7月9日債款約85%，墨西哥整體通膨也低於預期。接下來的美國PCE與7年期標售，將檢驗美債漲勢擴大後能否維持。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil's Decline Extends the Treasury Rally Beyond the Front End

Treasuries rallied across maturities Wednesday as more oil tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz and recovering energy exports eased concern about a lasting supply shock. The five-year yield fell 10 basis points to 4.17%, leading the move; the 10-year dropped 9 to 4.41%. Oil lost about 4% despite a large draw in US crude inventories, while disappointing housing indicators added evidence of cooling in an interest-sensitive part of the economy.

The rally reached further than Tuesday's two-year-led gain. Ten-year real yields fell 6 basis points to 2.23% and breakeven inflation declined 3 to 2.18%, so both components now contributed to the nominal move. The two-year fell a smaller 5 basis points to 4.11%, and the curve flattened. A $70 billion five-year auction found substantial investor demand without interrupting the rally.

Companies continued to borrow at a record pace. June US investment-grade issuance reached $175 billion, already exceeding the previous June record and dealers' forecasts, with more large technology deals being prepared. The volume concealed wide differences in terms: Hertz sought payment-in-kind convertible funding, Shapoorji Pallonji asked for extensions, and Antolin offered creditors a choice between waiting longer and accepting a principal reduction. Lower Treasury yields helped high-grade bond returns, but high-yield funds were almost flat.

## Five-Year Buyers Take Down Supply as Real Yields Fall

The five-year Treasury led both the two-year and the long bond, whose yield fell 8 basis points to 4.86%. The 2s10s slope narrowed 4 basis points to 30, and 2s30s narrowed 3 to 75. That reversed Tuesday's steepening, when buyers had concentrated in the front end. Five- and seven-year real yields fell 5 and 6 basis points, to 1.98% and 2.09%; 20- and 30-year real yields declined 6 and 5, to 2.53% and 2.71%.

The economic news gave the move support beyond oil. May new-home sales disappointed and building permits were weaker than expected. Housing alone did not establish a broad downturn, but it offered a domestic reason for investors to accept lower real yields after the previous day's business surveys had shown faster activity alongside weaker employment. The smaller two-year move still left room for further Fed restraint.

Treasury's $70 billion five-year note stopped at 4.200%, with a 4.125% coupon and 2.35 bid-to-cover. Indirect bidders took $43.028 billion and direct bidders $17.820 billion, leaving primary dealers $9.006 billion of competitive awards. The allocation showed substantial investor participation in the large sale.

Shorter securities also found demand. The $28 billion floating-rate reopening cleared at a 0.079% high discount margin and a 0.103% spread, with 2.99 cover. Indirect bidders took $18.650 billion, dealers $9.331 billion and direct bidders none. A $69 billion 119-day bill stopped at a 3.770% discount rate, equivalent to a 3.871% investment rate, with 2.55 cover. Its $37.414 billion of indirect awards exceeded the $28.495 billion dealer allocation.

Four- through 13-week bill yields were unchanged. The 17-week coupon-equivalent yield rose 2 basis points to 3.87%, while 26- and 52-week yields eased 1 and 2 basis points to 3.94% and 3.98%. The floating-rate note settles June 26; the 119-day bill and five-year note settle June 30. Bidding was orderly, with the associated cash transfers still ahead.

A Federal Reserve economist's study described a larger structural exposure behind Treasury liquidity. The repo-financed cash-futures basis trade accounted for an estimated $830 billion, or 35%, of hedge funds' long Treasury exposure in September 2025. Their gross Treasury exposure had doubled in two years to $4 trillion, with the 50 largest funds controlling 90%. Such large, concentrated positions can make a margin or volatility shock disruptive even when ordinary auctions clear comfortably.

## Record High-Grade Supply Meets a Harder Market for Stressed Borrowers

US investment-grade issuers have sold $175 billion in June, 60% more than in all of June 2025 and above the previous June record set in 2020. Nvidia and SpaceX each supplied $25 billion. Dealers had forecast about $130 billion for the month; the total could still exceed $200 billion. Year-to-date issuance reached $1.15 trillion, matching the comparable 2020 pace. Tight spreads have helped offset higher benchmark rates, while the prospect of Fed increases gives issuers a reason to borrow early.

The pipeline remained substantial. NTT was preparing roughly $10 billion of multi-currency bonds, and ByteDance was considering an offshore loan of about $20 billion as it weighed up to $70 billion of AI spending this year. Neither plan had final terms or a demonstrated order book. SK Hynix chose equity, planning 45.45 trillion won, or $29.4 billion, of Nasdaq-listed depositary receipts with trading expected July 10. That route limits the immediate need for more debt, even as the investment cycle keeps expanding.

The New York Fed's June Corporate Bond Market Distress Index update also pointed to generally functioning markets. The market-level measure improved and was slightly above its historical 20th percentile; investment-grade functioning was around the 50th percentile and high-yield distress remained historically low. The index combines primary-market activity with secondary liquidity and traded-versus-nontraded bond measures. It provides a broader view than the day's ETF moves: LQD rose 0.46%, while HYG and JNK slipped 0.03% and 0.06%.

Some buyers were accepting less liquidity for additional income. Among more than 400 Clearwater Analytics corporate clients managing about $1 trillion, the median treasurer held 2% in Rule 144A bonds, up from almost zero several years earlier. The average premium over comparable public high-grade bonds was about 52 basis points. Even cash-focused portfolios were moving further into that market.

### Refinancing Terms Reveal the Strain

Hertz paired a planned $300 million convertible payment-in-kind note with $100 million of stock intended to be shorted by convertible investors. Part of its revolving facility expires in June, and paying interest in additional debt would conserve cash. Its shares fell 41% after it warned that second-quarter adjusted earnings would be no more than $80 million. The package offered funding at the cost of potential dilution and a growing future debt obligation.

Shapoorji Pallonji Group offered a 30-basis-point consent fee to extend 143 billion rupees of zero-coupon bonds at least one month beyond June 30. It also sought to extend a Porteast Investment debt condition to September, after the loan-to-value cap on a separate $3.4 billion loan had temporarily risen to 40% from 34%. Borrowing is backed by the group's 18.4% stake in Tata Sons, making collateral value central to the negotiations.

The existing debt was already expensive. Goswami's zero-coupon notes originally yielded 18.75% when issued in 2023, then India's largest high-yield sale. Outstanding principal had fallen to 83.42 billion rupees while the yield rose to 21.75%. Porteast's $3.4 billion borrowing priced at 19.75% and was held by Ares, Cerberus, Davidson Kempner, Farallon and Deutsche Bank, among others. Most lenders supported the extensions, but Ares was still negotiating. The consent fee had not secured unanimous agreement.

Antolin offered two routes on more than €1 billion, or $1.1 billion, of debt. Creditors could retain par claims due in 2035 with a 6.97% coupon and no amortization, or take a 2030 maturity and an 8.28% coupon on only 67.5% of their current bond face value. Bank lenders keeping full principal also had to contribute toward €220 million of new working capital. Preserving the claim meant waiting longer; accepting a write-down brought earlier repayment and a higher coupon.

Infrastructure borrowers continued to secure private capital against physical assets. Terawatt arranged a five-year senior secured charging-site facility of up to $300 million, initially $150 million with an equal expansion option, for customers including Waymo. BloombergNEF estimates global charging networks need more than $635 billion through 2040. Stonepeak separately placed about $2.5 billion of private bonds to refinance construction financing for a Louisiana LNG export terminal in which it had agreed to buy 40%. Both financings still depend on development, utilization and completion, even with identifiable assets behind them.

## Central Banks Keep Tightening in View as Energy Pressure Eases

ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said further increases would probably be needed to return inflation to 2%, with timing and size dependent on the conflict, growth and prices. Spot energy prices remained above prewar levels and forward costs were elevated, she said. Christine Lagarde's view that a more forceful response was not yet needed left room for measured action rather than an accelerated campaign.

Germany's ifo business-climate index edged up to 85.6 from 85.0. Current conditions improved and expectations became less pessimistic, although manufacturing orders fell again. Services, trade and construction improved unevenly. The survey offered relief from immediate recession concern while giving little evidence of a strong recovery.

Japan's June meeting summary set out a clearer preference for continued normalization after the 7-1 vote to raise the policy rate to 1%, its highest since 1995. Members cited accommodative conditions and underlying inflation near 2%. One put neutral near 2%, within the bank's estimated 1.1%-2.5% range; another favored considering increases every few months. Governor Kazuo Ueda warned inflation could exceed target and tied the pace to economic, price and financial conditions. The yen remained near multidecade lows despite the increase, keeping imported inflation and possible intervention in view.

Australia's Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser argued that faster tightening could reduce inflation at a smaller employment cost now that the economy was on a steeper portion of the Phillips curve. The RBA had paused at 4.35% after increases at its first three meetings of the year. Its forecasts still put inflation at the midpoint of the 2%-3% target only in mid-2028, with unemployment peaking at 4.7%, leaving another increase possible.

The Bank of Korea pointed to housing and credit as well as prices. With its rate at 2.5% since the second half of 2025, it said an increase would be needed at an appropriate time as Seoul-area home prices, household debt and leveraged investment rebuilt imbalances. Banks and nonbanks retained regulatory capital and liquidity buffers. The concern centered on vulnerable borrowers and nonbank funding if leveraged asset prices reversed, requiring coordination with prudential policy.

Singapore and Thailand faced less immediate pressure. Singapore's May core inflation held at 1.4%, below the 1.6% survey estimate, supporting a July hold after April's monetary tightening and an increase in the 2026 core forecast range to 1.5%-2.5%. Thailand was expected to keep its one-day repo rate at 1% after May inflation eased to 2.79% and the currency remained relatively stable. Its central bank had previously waited through supply-led inflation before raising rates.

Canada's deliberations highlighted the risk of acting too late or too soon. First-quarter real GDP contracted at a 0.1% annualized pace after a 1% fourth-quarter decline, but more than half of industries expanded and consumer spending rose. Policymakers judged the weakness too limited to constitute recession. The Bank of Canada held at 2.25%, with core measures near 2% and limited energy pass-through. Raising rates after oil had normalized could prove unnecessary; persistent pass-through would make delay costly.

European governments obtained limited flexibility for energy-resilience investment under an escape clause originally intended for defense. The 3% deficit ceiling and country-specific expenditure paths remained. Ratings analysts viewed the move as bounded rather than a credit rupture, but it arrives as global sovereign borrowing is projected at $14.1 trillion in 2026, the ECB reduces holdings and Dutch pensions cut long-duration exposure. Investors will still have to absorb the resulting supply.

## Argentina Builds Cash for July; Mexican Inflation Undershoots

Argentina had accumulated about $3.6 billion in Treasury dollar deposits against a $4.2 billion bond payment due July 9, covering roughly 85%. Economy Minister Luis Caputo assembled hard currency at an average cost of 6.7%, below roughly 9% for a current international-market deal and about 10% several months earlier. Local dollar placements, central-bank purchases and multilateral-backed financing gave the government alternatives to an immediate global bond sale.

The cheaper funding still leaves maturities to manage. Local dollar bonds mature in 2027 and 2028, while peso auctions have carried fixed rates near 20%, or real rates around 7%. A decree authorizes up to $5 billion of dollar borrowing backed by institutions including the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank, with an estimated cost near 6%; authorization is separate from receipt of the funds. Country risk had fallen to around 430 basis points, at least 100 below earlier levels, improving the economics of a possible eventual market return.

Mexico's first-half June inflation undershot forecasts. Headline prices rose 3.55% over a year against a 3.72% median estimate; core eased to 4.12%, close to the expected 4.13%. Most of the downside surprise was therefore outside core. With the policy rate at 6.50% and the 2026 growth forecast cut to 1.1% from 1.6%, the figures gave Banxico more room to wait, although underlying inflation remained firm.

Chile held at 4.5% after a large fuel-price increase had pushed inflation above target. May prices rose 0.2% monthly, half the surveyed pace, and officials still expected a return to 3% inflation in the second quarter of 2027. India's 10-year government yield fell 5 basis points to 6.82% after the RBI governor called discussion of hikes premature. Rainfall remained a risk: the monsoon deficit was 43% through June 22, leaving food prices exposed.

Pimco saw a longer-term source of support for local EM bonds in China's manufacturing surplus. Trade barriers were redirecting Chinese exports toward developing economies, where cheaper goods could lower inflation and create room for rate cuts. The firm favored Latin America, particularly Brazil, Colombia and Peru, alongside high real yields and orthodox policy frameworks. The benefit to import prices comes with competition for domestic manufacturers, and dollar strength can still outweigh it. On Wednesday, EMB gained 0.32% as lower Treasury yields offset a modestly firmer dollar.

## Tanker Traffic Matters More Than the US Crude Draw

WTI fell 3.92% to $70.34 and Brent dropped 4.33% to $73.74, extending monthly declines to 27.18% and 28.78%. More tankers crossed Hormuz as the US and Iran reported progress in talks. UAE exports had recovered to nearly 85% of prewar levels in early June, and Qatar expected undamaged LNG capacity to return to normal within weeks. Negotiations remained unsettled, but the physical recovery gave investors more than a diplomatic headline to price.

The EIA reported a 6.1 million-barrel draw in commercial crude to 412.1 million barrels, about 7% below the five-year seasonal average. Product inventories moved the other way: gasoline rose 2.1 million barrels and distillates 3.1 million as refinery utilization reached 96.1%. Four-week gasoline demand was 3.0% lower than a year earlier, even while total products supplied rose 2.1%. Those details helped temper the crude draw's apparent signal of scarcity.

Equity losses were modest after Tuesday's rout. The S&P 500 fell 0.10%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.43% and semiconductors eased 0.18%; VIX declined 4.41% to 18.63. The Treasury rally broadened while demand for equity protection eased, consistent with energy relief rather than a new wave of recession fear.

The dollar index rose 0.20% to 101.61, up 1.52% over a week. Gold fell 3.38% to $3,990.30, while copper lost 1.9% to $13,117.50 a ton as dollar strength and hawkish Fed expectations weighed on metals. Falling Treasury yields did not bring a weaker dollar or a broad rebound in commodities.

## PCE and Seven-Year Supply Follow the Belly's Rally

May PCE inflation, personal income and spending, durable-goods orders, the third estimate of first-quarter GDP and initial claims arrive June 25 at 8:30 ET. After housing disappointed and real yields joined the Treasury rally, the inflation and spending figures will help show whether that broader demand for duration has support beyond cheaper oil. Persistent core-price pressure would put the largest gains in the belly under closer scrutiny.

Treasury sells $70 billion of four-week and $75 billion of eight-week bills at 11:30 ET, followed by $44 billion of seven-year notes at 13:00. A buyback of 20- to 30-year nominal coupons runs from 13:40 to 14:00; the auctions settle June 30. Participation and dealer awards will provide the next comparison with Wednesday's five-year result, before the later settlement cash flows.

The ECB Economic Bulletin is due June 25 at 10:00 CEST, Banxico announces at 15:00 ET with its overnight rate at 6.50%, and preliminary June Tokyo CPI follows June 26 at 8:30 JST. They will add detail on European energy pass-through, Mexico's response to softer headline inflation and the price outlook behind Japan's continued normalization.
